title: World Health Organization total alcohol consumption per adult
publisher: World Health Organization, Global Health Observatory
coverage: Countries/territories, 2000–2024 in the saved data interface extract; ages 15+, both sexes combined.
measure: Estimated litres of pure alcohol per person aged 15+, three-year averages, adjusted for unrecorded alcohol and tourism.
note: Public portal coverage metadata lags the saved data extract. These are estimates, not annual individual observations; the 2024 Australian estimate repeats 2023. Natural Earth provides the map geometry, not the alcohol values.

title: World Health Organization heavy episodic drinking by sex
publisher: World Health Organization, Global Health Observatory
coverage: Latest extract year 2020, country/sex estimates; population aged 15+.
measure: Age-standardised percentage consuming at least 60 grams of pure alcohol on one occasion in the past 30 days.
note: Denominator includes abstainers. The box plot weights countries equally and is not the distribution of individual drinkers. Its threshold differs from National Drug Strategy Household Survey measures.

title: National Drug Strategy Household Survey: alcohol
publisher: Australian Institute of Health and Welfare
coverage: People 14+ in private households; national age series 2001–2022–23, state snapshot 2022–23.
measure: Daily drinking; more than 4 standard drinks in a day at least monthly; more than 10 drinks per week; combined risky drinking. Tables 4.5,4.27,4.31 and 9b.16.
note: Each survey wave samples different people. Original unreliable flags are retained; unsuitable/suppressed values are null. Mosaic geometry alone is normalised for rounding. Table 4.31 has reversed footnote definitions; explicit weekly row labels were used and checked against marginal totals. The 2025 release available during research covers nicotine, rather than replacement alcohol tables.

title: National Health Survey: alcohol by age and sex
coverage: Australia 2022; the chart uses adults 18+ in seven age groups.
measure: Percentage exceeding the Australian Adult Alcohol Guideline 2020, Table 7.3. Reliability information checked against Tables 7.2/7.4.
note: National Health Survey differs from National Drug Strategy Household Survey in sampling and collection. Their estimates are not combined as interchangeable observations. The source reports sex categories as males/females.

title: Australian Secondary Students’ Alcohol and Drug Survey
publisher: Australian Government Department of Health; Cancer Council Victoria and research partners
coverage: School students aged 12–17,2022–23. Table 2, printed page 6/PDF page 9.
measure: Weighted ever, past-year, past-month, past-week and risky-past-week prevalence; all-student and age/gender subgroups.
note: Ever drinking includes even part of a drink. Risky past week means five or more drinks on any day. School participation was low and administration changed from previous waves; students do not represent all adolescents. Other/not-stated genders are omitted from the published breakdown because of small cell sizes. Waffle cells are percentage units, not respondents.

title: Alcohol available for consumption in Australia
publisher: Australian Institute of Health and Welfare; continuation of the former Australian Bureau of Statistics series
coverage: Total pure-alcohol availability 1960–61 to 2023–24; beverage shares shown 2011–12 onwards.
measure: Pure-alcohol supply per person aged 15+ (Table 7), and beverage-specific pure-alcohol volumes (Tables 1,3,5,6). Volumes are in thousands of litres.
note: Availability is supply, not individual self-report. It is not adjusted for all wastage, cooking or cellaring. Early beverage subtotals have discrepancies; the composition chart starts where source components reconcile within rounding. No source values are replaced to force agreement.

title: Alcohol-induced deaths
publisher: Australian Bureau of Statistics, Causes of Death Australia 2024
measure: Alcohol-induced death counts and age-standardised rates per 100,000. Waterfall changes are successive count differences.
note: Recent years are revised/provisional;2024 is preliminary. Registration year is not occurrence year. This narrowly coded measure is not all alcohol-attributable mortality. The May 2026 revision release does not publish replacement alcohol-specific tables; it was checked during research. Next advertised release:27October 2026.

title: Alcohol and other drug treatment services
publisher: Australian Institute of Health and Welfare
coverage: Eight state/territory jurisdictions,2015–16 to 2024–25; state Table.6.
measure: Closed treatment episodes for own drug use, where alcohol is the principal drug of concern.
note: Episodes are not unique clients; repeated treatment and service access affect counts. State populations differ. Geographic symbol positions are representative state anchors, not clinic locations; Australian Capital Territory is offset for readability.

title: Alcohol-attributable disease burden
publisher: Australian Institute of Health and Welfare, Australian Burden of Disease Study 2024
coverage: Australian 2024 modelled estimates by linked disease and sex; Australian Burden of Disease Study, Table 1.
measure: Disability-adjusted life years: healthy life years lost through early death and illness, attributable to alcohol.
note: Only mutually exclusive top-level groups are summed; their child rows are excluded. The five listed groups do not exhaust the reported total. ‘Not itemised here’ is an explicitly derived residual of total minus those groups (9,860 for all people); no disease composition is inferred. Bars show each group’s contribution to alcohol-attributable burden.

title: Alcohol-related hospitalisations
publisher: Australian Institute of Health and Welfare, National Hospital Morbidity Database
coverage: Australia 2023–24 joint age/sex data; National Hospital Morbidity Database, Table 3.
measure: Hospitalisation episodes with alcohol-related principal diagnoses, by age and sex.
note: Counts are episodes, not unique patients or population risk. The 55+ band is open-ended. Published totals include under 15/unknown age and other/unknown sex outside displayed bars. This extract provides no state breakdown. Revised diagnostic groupings are retained.
